findings.title: resolve_project_matrix non-ACTIVE 409 branch has no test
findings.why_it_matters: An admin can bind a RECORD matrix and later have it go non-ACTIVE (DRAFT/PENDING/OBSOLETE). When that project's users then submit-approval or approval-step, the contract promises a loud 409 SIGNATURE_MATRIX_NOT_ACTIVE instead of a silent fallback or a misleading 422 RECORD_APPROVAL_MATRIX_NOT_BOUND. That 409 branch is new in this batch, is reachable from both records_actions.py call sites, and nothing pins it: repo-wide grep shows the only two SIGNATURE_MATRIX_NOT_ACTIVE assertions target bind_to_project (422) and ensure_change_notice_matrix (409), not resolve_project_matrix. The branch (or its status code / error code) can be broken or changed while the whole suite stays green. A test parallel to test_project_without_record_matrix_is_422 closes the gap: bind a PENDING matrix, POST submit-approval, expect 409 + code.
findings.suggested_fix: In tests/api/v1/test_record_approval_chain.py add a red-first test next to test_project_without_record_matrix_is_422: create a matrix with status="PENDING", bind_to_project(module="RECORD"), then POST submit-approval and assert 409 with code SIGNATURE_MATRIX_NOT_ACTIVE (and optionally the same for approval-step). Optionally also cover the dangling-binding branch (binding row present, matrix row deleted) asserting 422 RECORD_APPROVAL_MATRIX_NOT_BOUND.

pcs-backend/app/services/signature_matrix_service.py:736-742 -- if matrix.status != "ACTIVE":

findings.title: Audit pagination tiebreaker fix shipped with no backend test
findings.why_it_matters: The batch's own convention is every fix lands with a red-first test, and commit 1fba41d's message repeats it — but the backend half of that commit (audit.py order_by tiebreaker) changed no backend test file. The fix's own comment names the user-visible failure: same-transaction audit rows (AD sync writes N rows with identical occurred_at) get unstable OFFSET pagination on Postgres, so the CSV export can contain a row twice and lose another, and the export row-count check the frontend added can never compensate because the frontend tests mock the backend. If the tiebreaker is reverted or reordered, tests/test_audit_query.py (test_pagination_limit_offset included) stays green. A test seeding rows with identical occurred_at and asserting the pages partition the set pins it.
findings.suggested_fix: In tests/test_audit_query.py add a test: insert ~5 audit rows all with the same occurred_at (distinct audit_ids), fetch page 1 (limit=2, offset=0) and page 2 (offset=2), assert the two pages are disjoint and their union equals the full filtered set — red against `.order_by(AuditLog.occurred_at.desc())` alone, green with the audit_id tiebreaker. Mirror the same ordering assertion for the config-audit endpoint (line 230).
evidence: pcs-backend/app/api/v1/audit.py:84-86 -- # ⚠️ **必须有 tiebreaker**（`audit_id`）：`occurred_at` 是 … 并列行的 OFFSET 分页在 Postgres 里 **顺序不稳定** ⇒ 同一行跨页出现两次、另一行永远不出现
git show --stat 1fba41d: pcs-backend/app/api/v1/audit.py | 14 ± — the only backend file changed; no pcs-backend/tests file in the commit (test additions were all pcs-frontend)
pcs-backend/tests/test_audit_query.py — 15 tests; test_pagination_limit_offset (line 180) paginates without equal occurred_at rows and never asserts ordering/tie stability

findings.title: resetMockSignState resets only sign state, not comments/admin seed
findings.why_it_matters: resetMockSignState() is the test-isolation seam for anything mounting signFlowHandlers, but it only restores mockSignSteps and mockDeliverableSignStatus. The disable handler mutates the shared exported seedAdminUsers objects in place (user.status = 'DISABLED'; user.token_version += 1) and the comments handler pushes into a module-level array that nothing resets. Vitest isolates per file, so today no test breaks — but the next test added to tests/mocks/signFlow.test.ts (or a new file reusing these handlers) that exercises admin disable or comment POST inherits earlier tests' mutations: generated comment_id (`c-${comments.length + 1}`) and user status/token_version become order-dependent, producing exactly the flaky by-order green/red this reset function was created to prevent.
findings.suggested_fix: Extend resetMockSignState() in src/mocks/signFlow.ts to also restore the other mutable state: rebuild comments from seedRecordComments.items (comments.length = 0; comments.push(...seedRecordComments.items)) and restore each seedAdminUsers entry's status/token_version (or snapshot originals at module load and re-apply; alternatively have the disable handler operate on a per-request copy). Rename not needed.
evidence: pcs-frontend/src/mocks/signFlow.ts:397-398 -- user.status = 'DISABLED';\n    user.token_version += 1;  (mutates the exported seedAdminUsers objects in place)
pcs-frontend/tests/mocks/signFlow.test.ts:71,128 — the only call sites of resetMockSignState, both as beforeEach isolation

residual_risks: Backend tests run against in-memory SQLite via conftest, not the Postgres the audit OFFSET-pagination comment targets; even after adding a tie test, cross-engine ordering guarantees are only truly exercised on Postgres (repo-known trap: a wrong migration stays green on SQLite).

Coverage-by-absence claims (untested branches) were established with repo-wide text grep over tests/ plus reading the relevant test files in full; a test exercising a branch without asserting its error code could have been missed, though the relevant suites assert codes everywhere else.
testing_gaps: ensure_default_record_matrix's dangling-binding repair branch (binding row exists, matrix row deleted → rebind the default matrix) is new in this batch and untested; test_ensure_default_record_matrix_does_not_override_existing_binding covers only the healthy-binding path.

POST /projects OpenAPI description promises full-transaction atomicity (建行 + 绑矩阵 + 建模板 same transaction, any failure rolls back); no test injects a mid-transaction failure to pin the no-half-built-project claim.
